bib.title: Data Manipulation with Pandas (Chapter 3, Python Data Science Handbook)

question: How does one use Pandas Series, DataFrame and Index, and its indexing, missing-data, MultiIndex, merge, groupby, pivot, string, time-series and eval/query tools, to manipulate tabular data?
contributions: Worked tour of Pandas 0.18.1 with real datasets: US states, Planets, Titanic, CDC births, OpenRecipes, Seattle Fremont Bridge, Google stock

Removed or changed since (from outside this source, check against current docs): .ix, Panel/Panel4D, DataFrame.append, concat join_axes, mean(level=), tshift, pd.datetime, sortlevel, MultiIndex labels (now codes), Int64Index, fillna(method=), drop(col, 1), pandas-datareader google source, old frequency aliases (H, T, S, L, U, N, A, BA).
The text itself flags eval/query as 'experimental' and gives no benchmark beyond one 87.1 vs 42.2 ms example.
Panel data, categorical dtype, nullable integer NA (only 'a proposal'), string dtype and Copy-on-Write are absent; string data is stated to be always object dtype.
Timings are single-machine %timeit best-of-3 with no variance.
practices: Use loc and iloc rather than [] or ix, especially with integer indices, to avoid the mixed explicit/implicit slicing convention (Data Indexing, Indexers).
Do not assign a column through attribute access (data.pop = z); use data['pop'] = z because names collide with methods.
Prefer fill_value in add()/sub() over NaN propagation when aligning mismatched indexes (Operating on Data).
Use isnull/notnull/dropna(how, thresh)/fillna rather than sentinels; remember integer columns upcast to float64 when NaN enters (Table 3-2).
Use a MultiIndex instead of tuple keys, and call sort_index() before partial slicing or you get a lexsort-depth KeyError (Hierarchical Indexing).
Use IndexSlice (pd.IndexSlice) for slices inside MultiIndex loc tuples.
Build a list of DataFrames and call pd.concat once instead of repeated append (Concat and Append).
After a merge, check isnull().any() to find unmatched keys, as done with PR and USA in the states example; use how='outer' first so nothing is silently dropped.
Use suffixes= for overlapping merge column names.
Use groupby aggregate/filter/transform/apply by intent: aggregate reduces, filter drops groups, transform keeps shape, apply is the general case.
Use pivot_table as the readable form of a two-key groupby plus unstack.
Use vectorized .str methods because they skip missing values where list comprehensions fail.
Use resample for aggregation and asfreq for selection when changing frequency; shift moves data, tshift moves the index.
Use query()/eval() for memory savings when temporaries approach RAM, not for speed on small data; use @name for local variables (eval/query section).
Use datetime64[ns] as the default date resolution.

a multidimensional version of GroupBy aggregation where split and combine happen across a two-dimensional grid
